title: Anthropic's $30 Trillion Bet, a Wrist-Worn AI Agent, and an Inbox on Autopilot
tldr: Anthropic is pushing toward a $2T IPO, but scrutiny is mounting over a two-quarter profitability claim (which excludes training costs) and a $30T market-opportunity projection.
Cal AI's founder debuted "Persona," a wrist-worn AI agent with a three-day battery that learns your habits and replies over text.
A simple Grok Bot workflow — with a ready-to-use prompt — turns your inbox into a prioritized, always-current action list.

tips.heading: Turn your inbox into an automatic, prioritized action list
steps: Open your AI agent (e.g. Grok Bot), connect your email account, and create a new agent dedicated to inbox triage.
Give it a standing job: scan recent emails, extract action items and deadlines, and ignore newsletters/spam.
Run it once, check accuracy, then save the process as a reusable skill or scheduled routine — keeping any send/delete actions gated behind your approval.
tips.prompt: Review emails from the last [24 hours/7 days]. Identify messages that require a reply, decision, follow-up, or task. Extract any deadlines and commitments. Create a prioritized action list with: Task, Sender, Deadline, Priority, Response Needed, and Source Email. Ignore newsletters, automated notifications, and spam. Do not send, delete, or modify any emails without my approval.

news.body: Anthropic is pressing ahead with a 2026 public listing at a reported $2T valuation, while two financial claims draw scrutiny: one report says it's been profitable for two straight quarters, but only when excluding training costs and shared revenue; Anthropic has also told investors it expects a $30T revenue opportunity — roughly 25% of today's global GDP — and is on track for $65B in annualized revenue this year. It also rolled out a Salesforce plugin with 37 sales-related skills.
news.means: Expect IPO headlines (and skepticism about the numbers behind them) to keep surfacing in client conversations about AI vendor stability and valuations.

news.body: Cal AI co-founder Zach Yadegari launched "Persona," a wrist-worn AI agent. Users talk to it by raising or tapping the wrist; it learns habits over time, replies via text, and runs about three days per charge.
news.means: A signal that consumer AI hardware is moving past phones and glasses to wearables — worth a mention if any client work touches wearables, health tech, or ambient computing.

news.body: A former Anthropic employee's warning that AI labs are "gambling with our lives" reignited the AI-safety debate. Doomer-side arguments point to incidents like OpenAI's Hugging Face breach as early warning signs; skeptics counter that today's models are still just fast pattern-matching software, and note labs pushing for regulation may benefit competitively from it.
news.means: Useful framing for client conversations about AI risk — most observers now agree both progress and safety matter, so calibrate messaging accordingly rather than picking a side.
